laws.rule: Tasmania Parks and Wildlife Service says visitors may not operate drones on reserved land, including national parks. The service may authorise certain commercial/event filming or scientific research; applicants need the specified CASA certification and licence before assessment.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: Tasmanian national parks and reserves have fuel-stove-only areas where campfires are prohibited all year or seasonally. The parks service lists Freycinet and Tasman national parks and much of the Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area, while noting some signed exceptions; check the site signs and current alerts.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: Tasmania Parks and Wildlife Service says firewood cutting and collection are not permitted in national parks and reserves. A total fire ban also prohibits outdoor solid and liquid-fuel fires, with limited electric and LPG cooker exceptions.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: Tasmania Parks and Wildlife Service says dogs and other pets are generally not allowed in national parks and reserves. Check permitted areas and contact the service about assistance dogs before visiting.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: A valid parks pass is required to enter Tasmania's national parks. A pass does not replace camping reservations or other separate fees; check the pass type and park details before travelling.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: Tasmania Parks and Wildlife Service says seasonal campfire bans began on 26 October 2026 in specified areas of reserved land. The listing and affected areas can change; check the current park alerts and fire-ban map before lighting a fire.
